messages:
marco_support: Hi team, customer reported inconsistent embedding vector lengths on bulk /v1/embeddings. Some batched items return 1536 dims, others 1. Happened intermittently with their integration. Customer request IDs: req=evb-20260317-01a, req=evb-20260317-01b. They've attached a minimal payload and a curl that reproduces it for them.

anya_eng: thanks. Can you paste the exact curl + payload and any server-side request ids/log snippets you have? Also which client library/version?

marco_support: here's what the customer used (sanitized key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  --data-binary @bulk.json
```
bulk.json is an array of documents, ~20 entries. The weird bit: when they gzip locally and send with Content-Encoding header, /some/ responses come back with embedding length 1 (instead of 1536). When they remove gzip and send raw JSON, the problem disappears.

devon_infra: interesting. Could be server mis-detecting boundary between requests in our batching layer if Content-Length isn't set or if gzip stream leaves trailing zero bytes. Do we log client_content_length vs actual_body_len?

marco_support: yes, I pulled logs for req=evb-20260317-01a from the edge proxy: 
```
[edge] req=evb-20260317-01a client_ip=1.2.3.4 client_content_length=0 transfer_encoding=chunked content_encoding=gzip
[proxy] forwarded_to=runtime node=rt-07 body_len=4096 decompressed=3987
[runtime] req=evb-20260317-01a batch_id=b-901 status=200 embeddings_count=20 embedding_dim_reported=1536
[runtime] req=evb-20260317-01a post_process warning=truncated_padding_bytes=\\u0000\\u0000\\u0000
```

marco_support: other request with issue (evb-20260317-01b) shows runtime returning embedding_dim_reported=1 and error=unexpected_input_shape. Log: 
```
[runtime] req=evb-20260317-01b batch_id=b-902 status=200 embeddings_count=20 embedding_dim_reported=1 error=kv-cache-unexpected-length
```

anya_eng: this smells like client-side gzip implementation that appends padding or uses a non-standard stream terminator; when edge reads chunked gzip and passes to runtime, our batch splitter may miscount token boundaries. Can we get the exact bulk.json (first 3 items) and a hexdump of the gzipped payload from the customer?

customer_jane: attaching minimal repro: first3.json and first3.json.gz (base64). I also included hexdump of first3.json.gz on my machine: "1f8b0800...00ff". I tried with python requests 2.31 and node fetch v3; both show same failure when gzipped. When I send plain json (no gzip) it always works.

anya_eng: thanks. Devon, can infra produce a debug bundle for those two request ids (evb-20260317-01a, evb-20260317-01b) and include raw edge body bytes and batch-split offsets? We need to confirm whether the boundary calc happened before or after decompression and whether trailing nulls were retained.
\
devon_infra: grabbing bundles now. gpt-deploy-bot, kick a bundle job.

gpt-deploy-bot: debug-bundle queued for [evb-20260317-01a, evb-20260317-01b]. S3: s3://redwood-debug/support/1845690123/gzip-body-batch-bundle.tar.gz (expires in 7 days).
\
anya_eng: pulled the bundle. Quick inspect shows edge recorded chunk sizes: 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 0 (terminator). However the last chunk contained 3 null bytes before terminator which our gzip wrapper kept. After decompression the runtime's tokenizer saw 3 null codepoints appended to the last text input which reduced effective tokenization and triggered an error path returning a degenerate embedding of length 1 for that example.
\
marco_support: so user payload had trailing nulls in the gzipped stream? How did they get there?
\
customer_jane: I re-ran hexdump and see the gz file contains extra 0x00 bytes right before gzip footer. My client library's streaming gzip writer pads the final chunk to 1024 bytes with zeros.
\
anya_eng: OK root cause: some gzip streamers pad the last chunk with nulls; our server's decompressor preserves those null bytes in decompressed text which can create unexpected token sequences for the tokenizer and in some cases cause the model to return a placeholder embedding (we surface as embedding length 1 / unexpected_input_shape). Fixes:
- Short term: advise customers to not send Content-Encoding: gzip or to ensure their gzip writer does not pad. Use --data instead of --data-binary for curl or use a non-streaming gzip.
- Medium: update edge to trim trailing null bytes after decompression for application/json content before tokenization. Add a sanitization pass.
\
devon_infra: created infra ticket INF-8721 to add post-decompress sanitization and to log when we remove NULs. Pushed a canary to rt-07.
\
marco_support: sent customer a repro note and suggested workaround. Customer confirmed that removing gzip fixed it. They asked whether this is a breaking change (they'll be switching to non-streaming gz lib). I told them we'll follow up after INF-8721 lands.
\
anya_eng: action items:
- dev: INF-8721 (trim NULs after decompress) 
- eng-runtime: add a regression test with padded gz streams (include python+node repro)
- support: flag any similar tickets and attach request ids to INF-8721
\
marco_support: marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if customer sees it again after workaround. :white_check_mark:
